'''Shiozakiyama Kofun''' (潮崎山古墳) is a {{ill|Kofun|en|Kofun|qid=Q1141225|lt=kofun}} located in {{ill|Shin'ichi|ja|新市町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shin'ichi, Hiroshima|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11502125}}, {{ill|Fukuyama, Hiroshima|en|Fukuyama, Hiroshima|qid=Q661038|lt=Fukuyama, Hiroshima}}, Hiroshima Prefecture, Japan. The mound is presumed to be a keyhole-shaped tumulus (前方後円墳) and is not designated as a historic site, but burial goods traditionally associated with the site — a '''Sankakuen shinjukyo (三角縁神獣鏡, triangular-rimmed deity-and-beast mirror)''' and an '''iron axe''' — are designated as '''Hiroshima Prefectural {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|qid=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property}}'''. The kofun is considered one of the earliest keyhole-shaped tumuli in the {{ill|Bingo Province|en|Bingo Province|qid=Q1049113|lt=Bingo Province}} region.

== Overview ==
[[File:潮崎山古墳出土 三角縁神獣鏡 (複製).JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Replica of the Sankakuen shinjukyo mirror (三角縁神獣鏡)}}{{small|On display at the '''{{ill|Hiroshima Prefectural Miyoshi Fudoki Hill|ja|広島県立みよし風土記の丘|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyoshi Fudoki-no-oka Museum|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11484763}}'''}}]]
Shiozakiyama Kofun is situated on a hill overlooking the confluence of the {{ill|Ashida River|en|Ashida River|qid=Q2577132|lt=Ashida River}} (芦田川) and Kamiya River (神谷川) in eastern Hiroshima Prefecture. The site was excavated in 1827 ({{ill|Bunsei|en|Bunsei|qid=Q1327119|lt=Bunsei}} 10, Edo period) and is recorded in the historical text {{ill|Q109361032|ja|西備名区|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saibimeiku|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q109361032}} (''Seibi Meiku''). However, no modern archaeological investigations have been conducted.{{Sfn|Shiozakiyama Kofun (古墳)|1989}}<ref name="sign"/>

The mound has been heavily altered and eroded, but based on estimates it was originally a keyhole-shaped tumulus with a total length of approximately 30 meters, with a rear circular section of 17 meters in diameter.{{Sfn|Shiozakiyama Kofun (古墳)|1989}} According to the historical records from ''Seibi Meiku'', the tomb likely contained a stone chamber (石槨, sekkaku).{{Sfn|Shiozakiyama Kofun (古墳)|1989}}

During the Edo-period excavation, a Sankakuen shinjukyo mirror (三角縁神獣鏡) and an iron axe were reportedly found. The tumulus is estimated to have been built in the 4th century during the early Kofun period, making it one of the earliest keyhole-shaped kofun in the Bingo region.{{Sfn|Shiozakiyama Kofun (古墳)|1989}}<ref name="sign"/>

The excavated mirror and iron axe were designated as Hiroshima Prefectural {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|qid=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property}} in 1981 and 1982. Today, a grave for Chiba Shuri-no-Shin (千葉修理之進) stands at the presumed rear circular section of the mound.

== Historic Site ==

=== Hiroshima Prefectural {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|qid=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property}} ===

* Important Cultural Property (Tangible Cultural Property)
** '''Sankakuen Goshin Shijukyo (三角縁五神四獣鏡) and Iron Axe (短冊型鉄斧)''' — Designated November 6, 1981 (Showa 56), expanded February 23, 1982 (Showa 57) to include additional burial goods.<ref name="hiroshima">[https://www.pref.hiroshima.lg.jp/site/bunkazai/bunkazai-data-202060060.html "Sankakuen Goshin Shijukyo & Iron Axe from Shiozakiyama Kofun"] (Hiroshima Prefectural Board of Education).</ref>
  ** '''Sankakuen Goshin Shijukyo mirror'''
    *** Diameter: 22.0 cm
    *** Thickness: 0.2–0.3 cm<ref name="hiroshima"/>
    *** Mold-identical in design to a mirror excavated from {{ill|Kokubunji Kofun (Kurayoshi)|ja|国分寺古墳 (倉吉市)}} in {{ill|Tottori Prefecture|en|Tottori Prefecture|qid=Q133935|lt=Tottori Prefecture}}.<ref name="sign"/>
  ** '''Iron Axe''' (短冊型鉄斧)
    *** Length: 24.8 cm
    *** Width at head: 5.5 cm
    *** Width at center: 6.0 cm
    *** Width at blade: 7.0–7.5 cm
    *** Thickness: 1–4 cm<ref name="hiroshima"/>

== Related Facilities ==
The replica of the mirror and other related burial goods from Shiozakiyama Kofun are exhibited at several museums:

* '''{{ill|Hiroshima Prefectural Miyoshi Fudoki Hill|ja|広島県立みよし風土記の丘|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyoshi Fudoki-no-oka Museum|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11484763}}''' (Miyoshi City) — Replica of the Sankakuen shinjukyo mirror and other burial goods.

* '''{{ill|Hiroshima Prefectural Museum of History|en|Hiroshima Prefectural Museum of History|qid=Q5771293|lt=Fukuyama Kusado Sengen Museum}}''' (Fukuyama) — Replica of the excavated mirror.

* '''Shin'ichi History and Folklore Museum''' ({{ill|Fukuyama Museum of History and Folklore|ja|福山市立しんいち歴史民俗博物館}}, Fukuyama) — Display of artifact replicas.
